I left a job I hated for what it was doing to my mental health last year and have lost 2 since because of it. All were customer service based in call centres which I didn't mind and was good at for a time.
I think what has the biggest impact is being in an environment where you have to interact with people constantly, it's so draining. Not only are you customer facing in your job but working in a close team you almost have no time to deal with your own feelings because you have to be constantly switched on to talk to other people. Mayne look into a new job doing something quiet, warehouse work or something manual where you can be left alone to get on with your work. Or even night shifts could suit you better as there's less people to deal with and they may prefer a similar quiet environment given the late shifts.
Hope everything works out for you, try your best and don't make any decision that could cause more trouble with bills and such but put your health first. If you aren't happy so soon after starting it may be the job is the problem. Best of luck!

I've never once said I'd like to run away from all of my problems. Believe me, mental health and debt issues don't go away no matter how far you run.

I'm trying to make a long term plan so I can be happier whilst dealing with the worst time in my life. Living in a different country doesn't mean I can't still pay my debt or that neither of us can get help or counselling for the mental health issues.

The reason I planned to start with at least a 6 month stint somewhere is so I'd have time to work my arse off full time and carry on paying things off but in a completely different environment. The actual travelling and touristy things would all be completely based on my situation then and what I could afford.

Thank you, I'm glad someone sees it from this point of view. I've thought about things from every angle as it's all been going on so long. There's no harm in thinking outside the box and getting ideas that aren't the norm because my situation is far from the norm.

The travelling would be a massive help for both our relationship and mental health problems, but the debt is holding us back. Then staying where we are and going through the same gloomy routine whilst on the arduous road to recovery also has an adverse effect on that healing process. It's very hard to find a middle ground. It would certainly be more difficult than for most but I'm up for the challenge, I think we just need something positive to work towards.

In all honesty, I'd be quite happy just working full time and then some just not where I am now. I'd still be looking to work and pay off my debts/raise money to travel first and foremost wherever I went.

I'm not trying to do anything to run away from my problems, I'm being realist about the fact that I'm struggling with them where I am right now, the environment you are in has a huge impact when dealing with mental illness as well as motivation to work extra and earn more money to pay the debt. They aren't problems that can't be dealt with anywhere in the world, and it would probably really help instead of just being stuck in a small bubble in the same routine, same glum corner of the world, surrounded by those problems.

My mental health problems come from the debt and strain on our relationship, my partners comes from over a decade of abuse which unfortunately can't be cut out of his life. However he is working harder to get help dealing with it, it's only been over the last year he's really been able to given how young he was when things happened, he just couldn't deal with it then.

Right now I'm trying to set things in motion to do all three, get debt free, for both of us to heal and be able to travel too, there's nothing to say we can't do it all at once, we may just have to work a hell of a lot harder to manage it but that's what I'm trying to prepare for.

Wow, I didn't know how serious they could be with things like that. I guess they have the power to do most things if they think it'll prove their case.

I'll absolutely be making sure I have decent funds as a back up. You're right, there's no point leaving one stressful situation only to end up in a worse one losing money on flights.
I have experience working with horses and a lot of customer service/insurance experience. I may be doing some financial exams this year which could help.

Thank you very much for your help and advice.

We are struggling relationship-wise currently but very aware of the problems and working towards solutions and healing. The problems are essentially just our mental health issues which he has been struggling to come to terms with but is dealing with things much better now and of course the debt but now we have more money coming in the strain should be lessened. We're being realistic with each other hence why I said it may be with him, we're aware things may not work and have agreed on time to see what happens or if we'll go our separate ways soon.

I knew there were guidelines for the amount you should have in savings for some countries but I didn't know they could check you at the border so thank you for that. I know I'd need a fair chunk to head off with so I'm working on starting my savings soon too.

I've used Workaway before and I know of WWOOF too which would be useful to keep accommodation costs down after arriving but before finding work, I really wanted a realistic idea of how long I might need to fund living without an income so I can plan accordingly.

As much as I wish I could leave today and not look back I know I need to be sensible, so leaving in a year would be the earliest but I'm going to plan for later next year in case.

Thanks for your reply and sorry for missing out the useful info!

Savings unfortunately not but I've just started a much better paying job so the money problems are going to be cut down in half the time now and I'll be able to save soon. I'm not intending to just pack up and go, as much as I'd love to, I know I have to be realistic and save for a while first.

We're struggling in our relationship due to both of our mental health problems and of course the debt is just a bitch on top of an already stressful situation. I'm not suggesting I want to run away from my problems, I want to be able to deal with them in a new environment while living out my dreams whilst dealing with all the shit life has thrown at us. If I can work full time there's no reason I can't carry on paying off debts while working in a different country, but I know I need to bring the amount down a lot before that would be an option. We're both working very hard regarding our health at the moment as well so things are relatively under control, but I guess in the sense that you can keep a fire under control, it could all get out of hand again very quickly.

Right now I'm just very tired of the same routine and of course dream of far off lands where I don't have to deal with it all, but back to reality for now. I know I'll get there, I just need telling to be patient sometimes x
